comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C25-C30 regarding the order-disorder transition model. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong experimental validation. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative agreement between model predictions and experimental measurements, while peer reviewers praise the 'convincing model' and 'new mechanism' for disordered patterning.

Complete agreement on claims C17-C20, C31 regarding basic experimental observations. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes them as 'well-documented descriptive findings,' while peer reviewers note the experimental techniques are 'presented quite clearly' though 'borrowed from earlier works.'

Disagreement on claims C21-C22 regarding prior modeling assumptions. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as accurate citations of established work, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether 25% Tip cells automatically imply salt-and-pepper patterns and noting lack of direct experimental validation.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claims C80-C81 regarding methodological assumptions. Both identify concerns about the binary Tip/Stalk classification and hexagonal lattice assumptions. Peer reviewers additionally raise concerns about cell size variability affecting the findings.

Significant disagreement on claims C8, C46-C50, C56 regarding fibronectin and Turing-like patterning. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with reasonable mechanistic inference despite correlative nature. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'very little evidence to support the hypothesis about a Turing-like mechanism' and finding the proposed mechanism 'somewhat unsatisfactory.'

Strong agreement on claims C35-C40 regarding sprout dynamics. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises the quantitative tracking data in Figure 4, while peer reviewers highlight the Sankey diagram analysis as 'quite novel' in the Notch signaling literature. Peer review also includes claims C5, C6, C74 about instability.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for claims C7, C41-C43 regarding sprout spacing models. Both accept the random uniform model's agreement with experimental data. OpenEval emphasizes systematic comparison of three models, while peer reviewers note the quantification of spacing statistics and partial recapitulation. Peer review also includes claims C54-C55.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for claims C32-C34 regarding disordered pattern validation. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation through nearest neighbor analysis, while peer reviewers accept the modeling approach and praise the 'quantification of Tip spatial patterns' as novel. Peer review also includes claims C23-C24 about bimodal distributions.

Both address modeling results with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval R7 focuses on claims C23-C24 regarding bimodal distributions from computational modeling. Peer R2 includes these claims along with C32-C34, praising the overall modeling approach and experimental validation as providing 'important new insight.'

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for claims C9, C51-C52, C72, C76-C77 regarding the mechanistic framework. Both accept the interpretation of NOTCH's enabling rather than instructive role. OpenEval notes the synthesis is 'reasonably inferred' though 'some aspects remain speculative,' while peer reviewers praise the careful distinction between assumptions and proven facts.

Partial overlap on claims C5-C6, C74 regarding Tip cell dynamics and instability. OpenEval R6 groups these with broader mechanistic framework (SUPPORTED), while peer R3 focuses on temporal dynamics C35-C40 (also SUPPORTED). Both evaluations are positive but emphasize different aspects of the dynamic behavior.

Partial overlap on claims C54-C55 regarding mechanistic inferences. OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN as 'proposed mechanisms that would require additional experiments to validate.' Peer R4 rates the broader set including C7, C41-C43 as SUPPORTED, focusing on the spacing model rather than the specific mechanisms in C54-C55.

Partial overlap on claims C76-C77 regarding contextualization with prior work. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as appropriate citations, while peer R6 focuses on the broader interpretive framework C9, C51-C52, C72 (also SUPPORTED). Both evaluations are positive about the contextualization.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claim C53 regarding two-cell sprout formation. OpenEval notes this is 'supported by occasional observations' but part of broader speculative mechanisms. Peer reviewers raise specific concerns that two-cell sprouts from early stage-I mechanism could affect inter-sprout distance statistics.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for claim C67 regarding comparison to C. elegans. OpenEval finds the comparison appropriately cited and contextualized. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'the authors did a good job' with this comparison and suggest extending to Drosophila tracheal patterning.

Partial overlap on claim C56 regarding fibronectin mechanisms. OpenEval rates C56 as UNCERTAIN within broader mechanistic inferences C53-C59, C78-C79. Peer R5 rates the fibronectin/Turing claims C8, C46-C50, C56 as UNCERTAIN, expressing stronger reservations about insufficient evidence for the Turing mechanism.
OpenEval R9 evaluates claims C1-C3, C10-C16 as SUPPORTED background knowledge from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.
OpenEval R11 evaluates claims C44-C45, C57-C58 as SUPPORTED citations of prior literature on fibronectin. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background citations.

OpenEval R13 evaluates claims C61-C65 as UNCERTAIN extrapolations to pathophysiological contexts. These are noted as 'speculative extensions' to disease contexts without direct validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R15 evaluates claim C60 as SUPPORTED citation of alternative models from recent literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific contextualization.
